title: Store, Actions, and Reducers
description: Learn the three core building blocks of Redux.

data.text: Redux has three core concepts that work together: the **Store** holds your state, **Actions** describe what happened, and **Reducers** specify how state changes in response. Once you understand how these three pieces interact, you have the mental model for every Redux application.

data.caption: How the Store, Action, and Reducer work together

flowchart TB

    style R fill:#e7ffe1

data.text: The **store** is the single object that holds your application's state and provides the methods to read it, change it, and listen for changes. In modern Redux you create it with `configureStore` from Redux Toolkit, but the underlying `createStore` API exposes the same essential methods.

data.title: Creating a Store

data.text: An **action** is a plain JavaScript object that describes what happened in your application. The only requirement is that it has a `type` field, which is a string that uniquely identifies the action. Other fields carry the data needed to update state.

data.title: Action Objects

data.text: Most apps wrap action creation in **action creator** functions. This keeps your code DRY and makes refactoring easier because the action shape lives in one place.

data.title: Action Creators

data.text: A **reducer** is a pure function that takes the current state and an action, and returns the next state. Reducers are the only place state transitions are defined, which makes them the heart of every Redux app.

data.title: Reducers Must Be Pure
data.text: Reducers must be pure functions - they cannot mutate state, perform side effects, or call non-pure functions like Date.now() or Math.random(). If you need side effects, use middleware or move them outside the reducer.

terms.definition: A string constant that uniquely identifies an action. Conventionally written as `domain/eventName` (e.g. `todos/add`).
A function that returns an action object. Helps avoid typos and keeps the action shape in one place.

A function that always returns the same output for the same input and has no side effects.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: The store holds state and exposes dispatch, getState, and subscribe
Actions are plain objects with a required `type` field
Action creators wrap action creation for reuse and consistency
Reducers are pure functions that return the next state
Reducers must never mutate state or perform side effects
data.takeaway: The store, actions, and reducers are the three foundational building blocks of every Redux application.
